title: Linking a Trade-In Agreement to a Kestrel Purchase
content:
An accepted offer under **Trade-In Agreements** may be tied to a Kestrel purchase order or left as an outright sale.

**The rule.** An accepted offer may be linked to one of the customer's own Kestrel purchase orders, or left unlinked as an outright sale when the grade allows outright sales. A trade is linked only to a purchase order of the same customer whose status is reserved or contracted (contracted being the trade link cutoff), and a purchase order may carry no more than the grade's maximum trade-ins per purchase. That count is the number of trade-in agreements linked to the purchase order whose status is accepted, picked up or settled, taken as it stands at the moment of the request. Equity from all trades linked to one purchase order is combined on that order as separate trade equity payments, one per trade. When the linked purchase order is paid through Kestrel Auto Finance, the trade's negative equity may be rolled into that finance contract under the negative equity rule of Trade-In Agreements; an unlinked trade, or a trade linked to a cash or outside-lender purchase, can only have its negative equity covered by customer payment.

The purchase order's status, its customer and its reference number are read from Kestrel's purchase records before the link is made.

### Which purchase orders can receive the link?

| Purchase order | Can the trade be linked? |
|---|---|
| Same customer, status reserved | Yes, subject to the count |
| Same customer, status contracted | Yes, subject to the count |
| Same customer, any later status | No |
| Another customer's order | No |

### How is the per-order count read?

Agreements linked to the order count when their status is accepted, picked up or settled. Offered, declined, expired and cancelled agreements do not count. Where the count already equals the grade's maximum trade-ins per purchase, no further trade is linked to that order.

### How does equity from two trades reach one order?

Each linked trade posts its own trade equity payment on the order; the two are combined on the order as two separate payments, never merged into one.

### How can negative equity be covered?

| How the linked purchase is paid | Coverage of negative equity |
|---|---|
| Kestrel Auto Finance | May be rolled into that finance contract under the negative equity rule |
| Cash | Customer payment only |
| Outside lender | Customer payment only |
| No linked purchase (outright sale) | Customer payment only |

### Illustration (hypothetical)

A contracted purchase order already carries one picked-up trade and one cancelled trade. The count is 1; a grade whose maximum trade-ins per purchase is 2 allows one more link to that order.
